human_tolerance.notes: Now one of the commonest thrushes in suburban parks, backyards and pastures across its range, helped enormously by nest-box programmes.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Winters in the southern United States and Mexico; most individuals leave the northern breeding range.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Arrives in spring; a mature female typically raises two broods, in a cup nest built in an abandoned woodpecker hole or other cavity, taking about 10 days to build, with 13 to 16 days of incubation and fledging 15 to 20 days after hatching.

vocalizations.description: A soft, liquid warbling song of a few warbled notes, given from a perch; both sexes also warble when predators are near.
A short, harsh, song-like cry given by the male when a predator approaches, usually with flicking of the wings.

range.note: Breeds in eastern North America and winters in the southern United States and Mexico; a resident population persists on Bermuda, which is not listed here.

traits.limb_count.note: Biped: two legs; the wings are not counted as limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Perches on fences, posts and wires and flies between them, dropping to the ground to take insects.

traits.nest_type.note: Nests in abandoned woodpecker holes or other cavities, usually several feet above the ground, in a small cup of grass, feathers, stems and hairs.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 27.5 g converted to kilograms; Wikipedia independently gives 27-34 g.

traits.length_m.note: Body length of 16-21 cm; the midpoint of that range is used.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of the 25-32 cm wingspan given on Wikipedia.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia gives 6 to 10 years, with a longest recorded lifespan of 10 years and 5 months; the midpoint of the stated range is used.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 70 mapped to 'invertebrate' and Diet-Fruit 30 to 'fruit'; the dataset classes this species as an insectivore that supplements its diet with fruit.

traits.social.note: A pair is the breeding unit; outside the breeding season it forms loose flocks, which are not counted here because no open source quantifies flock size.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal 0; Wikipedia describes a diurnal bird active from dawn.

traits.defense.note: Drops away from an approaching predator and gives a warning cry; judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: it watches from an exposed perch and drops out of reach rather than flying far, so it is moderately wary but tolerant of places with people, such as pastures and backyards.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value records this species as 100% ground-foraging, which matches the perch-and-drop feeding described on Wikipedia; a small arboreal share is retained for its use of nest cavities and tree cover, and is judgement.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the nesting weights are judgement, since no open source gives the relative importance of natural cavities and nest boxes.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia describes it as now most common along pastures, agricultural fields, suburban parks, backyards and golf courses.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia calls it a migratory thrush that winters in the southern United States and Mexico.

seasonal.phases.note: Nest-building time, two broods per season, incubation and fledging intervals and the cavity nest are from Wikipedia's breeding section; the three calendar windows are authored judgement, since no open source gives arrival and departure dates for the northern states.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Fledging is 15 to 20 days after hatching, giving the 35-day juvenile window; the 0.85 scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.song.note: Wikipedia states that both sexes flick their wings and warble when predators are nearby and that the male gives a song-like warning cry; the quiet warbling song attributed here is authored, and the months, time windows and cooldown are authored judgement. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

vocalizations.warning_cry.note: Wikipedia states the male makes a song-like warning cry when approached by a predator; the wording and cooldown here are authored.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description of the male: deep blue upperparts with a rust-orange throat and breast and a white belly. The proportions and the rufous breast box are authored judgement to render the orange breast.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: it drops 8 m from a threat, hunts insects, warbles and gives the warning cry, and nests in cavities between March and June.
